sentences.text: Dimati Devi vs The State Of Uttarakhand on 12 June, 2024

Author: Vikram Nath
Bench: Vikram Nath
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal Nos.11581159 Of 2015
 Dimati Devi Etc. Appellant(S)
 Versus
 State Of Uttarakhand Respondent(S)
 Order

1. The appellants Dimati Devi and Yashwant Singh (mother and son) are before this Court assailing the correctness of the judgment and order dated 26.06.2013 passed by the Division Bench of the Uttarakhand High Court whereby the criminal appeals preferred by the appellants against their conviction under section 302/34 Indian Penal Code, 18601 have been dismissed.

entities.text: Division Bench of the Uttarakhand High Court
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Initially, the First Information Report 2 was lodged under sections 304B, 498A and 120B IPC and section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,19613 alleging that the wife of Yashwant Singh had died an unnatural death on 07.05.2007.

The postmortem was conducted on 09.05.2007 according to which there were no signs of external injury however 4th and 5th cervical vertebrae were found fractured and hyoid bone was also found fractured.
The cause of death was ascertained as neurogenic shock caused by ante mortem injuries on the neck.
Chargesheet was submitted under sections 304B and 120B IPC as also section 3/4 of 1 IPC 2 FIR 3 DP Act the DP Act that is to say that section 498A IPC was dropped.
3. The Trial Court however framed an alternative charge under section 302/34 IPC also.

After a full trial, the Trial Court acquitted the appellants under section 304B IPC as well as section 3/4 of the DP Act but convicted them under section 302/34 and 120B IPC and awarded life sentence with fine of Rs.5,000/ on each of the appellants under section 302/34 IPC and further fine of Rs.5,000/
under section 120 B IPC.
4.

It has been stated at the bar that Dimati Devi motherinlaw of the deceased has undergone nine years of incarceration and presently on bail whereas the other appellant Yashwant Singh has throughout remained in custody and has undergone more than 17 years of incarceration.
It is also an admitted case that the husband of the deceased Yashwant Singh was serving in the Indian Army.

sentences.text: The High Court relied upon Modis Medical Jurisprudence and Toxicology, 22nd Edition (page 423) and reproduced the paragraph under heading Concussion of the Spine as:

entities.text: Modis Medical Jurisprudence and Toxicology, 22nd Edition (page 423)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Concussion of the Spine may occur without any evidence of an external injury to the spinal column.

It may follow a severe blow on the back, or a jar, or a fall from a height, or a bullet injury and had arrived at the conclusion that it was not a case of severe blow on the back or fall from a height or a bullet injury but was a result of Jar.

The High Court also noticed that the appellants failed to discharge their burden under section 106 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 to explain as to how the death has been caused which fact could have been in their exclusive knowledge only.

6. Learned counsel for the appellants had sought to argue that relying only upon the medical evidence the conviction has been recorded and once the Trial Court had acquitted of the charges of Dowry death and during investigation the charge of demand of dowry and harassment on such account having not been found, the conviction is bad in law.
It is further submitted that there was no evidence of common intention and conspiracy.

7. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for respondent State of Uttarakhand submitted that the husband of the deceased was in the Army and was well trained in causing the Jar as a result of which both the cervical vertebrae and hyoid bone would be fractured.
It is for this reason that no external injury has been found in the neck either in the front or the back.
He further submitted that Trial Court and the High Court have rightly convicted both the appellants.

8. Having considered the submissions made on behalf of the parties and having perused the material on record, we find that there was no evidence to find any common intention of the mother and son in committing the crime.
Further there is no evidence to prove the alleged conspiracy.

Once the dowry demand or any harassment on that account was not charged and further also dowry death having not been proved before the Trial Court, the only evidence was with regard to culpable homicide amounting to murder.

There is no evidence of any other external injuries on the body of the deceased, therefore, it cannot be presumed that the motherinlaw of the deceased also had an active participation, common intention and had conspired in the commission of the crime.
Insofar as the husband of the deceased is concerned, we find no reason to interfere with the conclusion arrived at by the Trial Court and the High Court in recording conviction.
9. In view of the above, we allow the appeal filed by Dimati Devi and after setting aside the conviction and sentence, she is acquitted of all the charges.
She is already on bail.
Her bail bonds are cancelled and sureties discharged.
Insofar as the appeal of Yashwant Singh, husband of the deceased is concerned, the same stands dismissed.

10. In case Yashwant applies for premature release/remission under the extant policy of the State,
the same would be considered and decided by the respondent State of Uttarakhand in accordance with law expeditiously, preferably within a period of three months.

Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
